 Judgment

The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.705 of 2009 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Irinjalakuda, is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 19.10.2008.

According to the petitioner, on 19.10.2008 at about 12.30 p.m., while he was travelling in the goods carrying autorickshaw bearing Registration No.KL-10/P 1138 as the owner of the goods, driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, he lost the control over the vehicle.
As a result of the accident, he fell down and sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.10,42,000/- limited to Rs.5,00,000/-.

4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the MACA NO. 1768 OF 2014 2025:KER:31205 accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PWs 1 and 2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A10 and B1.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,56,960/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9. Heard Sri.P.V.Baby, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.P.Muraleedharan, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.

2 10.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
As per the claim petition, the petitioner was working in a petrol pump earning Rs.4,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his MACA NO. 1768 OF 2014 2025:KER:31205 monthly income at Rs.3,500/-.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2008 will come to Rs.6,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned counsel prayed for fixing the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.6,500/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

Since the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2008 will come to Rs.6,500/-, in order to award just and reasonable compensation, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra), the notional income of the petitioner is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.6,500/-.
12.
In the accident the petitioner sustained severe contaminated crush wound in (L) foot with non viable big toe 2 nd and middle toes and those were amputated.
Further managed with wound debridement and flap cover with anterio lateral thigh flap, again admitted for debulking of the lateral 3/4th and medial side.
Further treated for excision of callosity of the left foot.
13. Ext.A6 disability certificate issued by PW2 shows that the petitioner suffered 24.18% permanent physical disability.
The Tribunal, however, scaled down the percentage of disability of the petitioner to 15%, MACA NO. 1768 OF 2014 2025:KER:31205 without assigning valid and cogent reasons.
The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or higher Authority.

(See Manikantan G. v.
Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305). Having not done so, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the percentage of disability from what is shown in the disability certificate.

entities.text:
Manikantan G. v.
Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I do not find any grounds to disbelieve the said disability and as such the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is fixed as 24.18%.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 47 years.

Therefore, 25% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 13, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.3,06,482/-.
15.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.21,000/- being the income for 6 months @Rs.3,500/-.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 9 months.

Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.58,500/-
(6500x 9 months).
MACA NO. 1768 OF 2014 2025:KER:31205 Preman vs Raneesh on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157849218/
3 16.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/-, towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.50,000/- and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.500/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
17. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 30 days in different spells.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.1,50,000/, Rs.1,50,000/- and Rs.10,000/-
respectively.
18. Towards the head 'bystander expense', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.4,500/-.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the head 'bystander expense' is on the lower side and hence it is enhanced to Rs.6,000/- (Rs.200 x 30 days).
19.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

The Tribunal directed the 3 rd respondent to pay the amount and recover the compensation from respondents 1 and 2 on the ground that at the time of the accident, 2nd respondent did not have a valid driving licence.
Though notice was served, respondents 1 and 2 did not turn up and did not produce the valid driving licence of the 2nd respondent.
Therefore, the permission granted to the third respondent to recover compensation from respondents 1 and 2 is retained.

21. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.7,50,042/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

22.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3 rd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.7,50,042/- (Rupees Seven Lakh Fifty Thousand Forty Two only) and permitted to recover the same from respondents 1 and 2, less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner,
excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
